*Do not edit this template directly. Instead, copy this Task, update the title, and fill in the relevant sections below.* All access requests must be tracked in Jira for security, compliance, and audit purposes. Requests made through Slack, email, or other ad-hoc channels are not considered valid unless captured here.

All approvals, decisions, and provisioning steps must be recorded in the created Task. Incomplete requests or missing approvals may delay or block access. *Access may be reviewed or revoked if it is no longer required.*

*HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE*

# Fill in all required sections. Failing to fill required section will result in delays in processing the request.
# Provide a business justification; explain clearly why this access is needed. Access is granted only when there is a concrete, work-related need.

# Once everything is in place ping {{@aipcc-support}} in {{#forum-aipcc}} slack channel for review.

----

*GENERAL REQUEST INFORMATION* (required for all requests)

* *Requestor's name*: Rastislav Papso
* *Requestor's Red Hat email*: rpapso@redhat.com
* *Organization and team*: AI Engineering, Agentic API Team
* *System(s) requested*: Quay

----

*QUAY / KONFLUX ACCESS REQUESTS*

Access to AIPCC-owned Quay repositories and Konflux tenants follows the same request and approval process and is granted at the same time. If you are unsure whether you need the access, do not request it. Requests without a clear justification may be denied. Any access beyond read-only requires both a business justification and manager approval.

Please provide:

* *Justification for access*: The Agentic API team uses the Quay registry to store container images of projects they are responsible for (i.e. OGX). As a new joiner to the team, I’ll need access to Quay to be able to work with published images.
* *Link to your MR*: [https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/service/app-interface/-/merge_requests/196349|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/service/app-interface/-/merge_requests/196349]

Instructions for creating the MR:

# Follow the workflow instructions outlined here: [https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/service/app-interface#workflow|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/service/app-interface#workflow].
# Add or update the relevant permission files with your user details.

# Once your MR is ready, paste the link into this Jira ticket. *The request will not be reviewed until the MR link is provided.*

items.fromString:
Add package 'rdkit' into the RHAI pipeline onboarding collection.

The package requires builder repository onboarding before it can be added to the RHAI pipeline. This ticket is blocked by the builder onboarding ticket.

h3. Summary
RDKit (complexity 9/10) has *no sdist on PyPI* and requires a full C++20 CMake source build with ~770 C++ files, Boost compiled from source via Conan, and numerous bundled native libraries — wheels are produced only through the third-party `kuelumbus/rdkit-pypi` build harness using cibuildwheel on manylinux_2_28. No critical blockers exist for x86_64 Linux/GCC, the BSD-3-Clause license is fully compliant, and *no CUDA/ROCm-specific builds are needed* since RDKit is CPU-only. Recommend adapting the rdkit-pypi containerized build pipeline immediately to validate the build environment ahead of the 2026-08-18 target date.

items.fromString:
Update the UCX RPM spec from v1.19.0 to v1.20.1 and build it with CUDA bindings for the cuda13.0-ubi9 base images.

h2. Motivation

The LLM-D team requires UCX 1.20.1. nixl depends on UCX for high-performance GPU-aware communication, and the updated version is needed for the RHELAI 3.5 GA base images.

h2. Scope

* Update the UCX spec file to version 1.20.1
* Ensure CUDA transport plugins are built (ucx-cuda, ucx-gdrcopy, ucx-ib, ucx-cma, ucx-rdmacm, ucx-ib-mlx5)
* Verify build with CUDA 13.0 headers
* Do a scratch build to validate

h2. References

* Upstream: https://github.com/openucx/ucx/releases/tag/v1.20.1
* Previous UCX build (v1.18.1): AIPCC-1902
* UCX transport sub-RPMs (v1.19.0): AIPCC-4765
* Brew build ticket: AIPCC-21322
* RPM how-to: https://gitlab.com/redhat/rhel-ai/core/team-docs/-/blob/main/docs/ecosystems/how-tos/rpm.md

Goal: _As a productization engineer, I want the ROSA HCP cluster pipeline to authenticate with an OCM service account, so that cluster management does not depend on any individual's personal credentials._

h3. Context

Commit [3afe44a|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ai/rosa-hcp-aipcc-arc/-/merge_requests/21] switched from an OCM service account ({{RHCS_CLIENT_ID}} / {{RHCS_CLIENT_SECRET}}) to kdreyer's personal offline token ({{RHCS_TOKEN}}) as a workaround for "Specified account is invalid" errors in the new AIPCC OCM org. We should revert that commit and use a service account in the AIPCC OCM org.

There’s a reference to the SA here: [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AIPCC-19495|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AIPCC-19495|smart-link] 

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* The RHOAI OCM org's original service account permissions are documented. 
* A service account exists in the AIPCC OCM org with equivalent permissions.
* GitLab CI/CD variables use RHCS_CLIENT_ID and RHCS_CLIENT_SECRET instead of RHCS_TOKEN.
* The README documents the service account variables.

[4849349873] Upstream Reporter: Lalatendu Mohanty
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}### Bug description

**Expected behavior:**
Error messages should not repeat the same information.

**Actual behavior:**
`resolver.py:286-288` wraps exceptions with `raise ResolverException(f"...{original_msg}") from err` ? embedding the cause's text in the outer message AND chaining it as `__cause__`. When `__main__._format_exception()` formats this, it appends `" because {cause}"`, producing a duplicated message:

```
Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1
  with constraint flashinfer-python==0.6.11.post2: found no match for
  flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 because found no match for
  flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1
```

The `" because found no match..."` portion is redundant ? the same text already appears after the colon.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Trigger any resolution failure where `find_all_matching_from_provider()` wraps a `ResolverException` with `from err` (the common case for constraint conflicts or missing packages).

### Proposed fix

Add a dedup check in `_format_exception()`: when the outer exception's message already starts with the cause's raw message (`str(exc.__cause__)`), skip the `" because ..."` clause. A `startswith` check matches the actual construction pattern (`f"...{original_msg}"`) without false-positiving on coincidental substrings.

This was originally part of #1241 but is being split out as an independent fix.{quote}

*Goal:* _As a build engineer, I want the ARC ROSA cluster to pull secrets from HashiCorp Vault automatically, so that credential management is consistent with our other deployments and secrets are not stored solely in GitLab CI variables._

*Background:* Our other OpenShift deployments ([k8s-gitlab-runner|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ai/k8s-gitlab-runner], dashboard, pruner) use the Vault Secrets Operator with AppRole auth against {{vault.corp.redhat.com}}. The ARC ROSA cluster currently stores the GitHub App credentials as [GitLab CI variables|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/ai/k8s-arc/-/settings/ci_cd#js-cicd-variables-settings] and applies them with kustomize in CI. Moving to VSO brings this cluster in line with the team pattern.

*Implementation:*

# Determine whether the existing {{ai-aipcc-cicd}} AppRole can be reused, or request a new one via [ServiceNow|https://redhat.service-now.com/help?id=sc_cat_item&sys_id=566f2caf1b5360107f9bfc8f034bcba7].
# Install the Vault Secrets Operator from OperatorHub on the cluster.
# Create injector-labeled {{trusted-ca-bundle}} ConfigMaps in each ARC namespace (see [AIPCC-21313|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AIPCC-21313]).
# Manually apply bootstrap resources on the cluster (not in Git, per team convention):
#* {{Secret}} with the AppRole secret ID
#* {{VaultConnection}} pointing to {{vault.corp.redhat.com:8200}}
#* {{VaultAuth}} with AppRole credentials

*For ARC’s GitHub app credential storage:*

# Esnure the GitHub App credentials (app ID, private key) from [AIPCC-18931|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AIPCC-18931] are in Vault under {{ai-aipcc-cicd/arc/github-app}} (or similar path).
# Add a {{VaultStaticSecret}} to {{k8s-arc}} that syncs the GitHub App credentials into a K8s Secret.
# Update the ARC Helm values to reference the VSO-managed Secret instead of the manually-created one.
# Add {{secrets.hashicorp.com}} permissions to the {{gitlab-ci-arc-deploy}} ClusterRole in {{ci/deploy-sa.yaml}}.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* The Vault Secrets Operator is installed and running on the cluster.
* VaultConnection and VaultAuth are configured and can authenticate to {{vault.corp.redhat.com}}.
* The GitHub App credentials are stored in Vault under {{ai-aipcc-cicd/}}.
* A VaultStaticSecret syncs the credentials into a K8s Secret in the {{github-arc-system}} namespace.
* ARC runner pods authenticate to GitHub using the VSO-managed Secret.
* The CI deploy SA has RBAC for {{secrets.hashicorp.com}} resources.

*Goal:* As a release engineer, I want the ARC ROSA cluster to trust Red Hat's internal CA, so that workloads (e.g. Vault Secrets Operator) can connect to internal TLS services over TGW.

*Background:* The ARC ROSA cluster has TGW connectivity to the RH internal network, but containers only trust public CAs by default. On ROSA, the supported path is {{rosa edit cluster --additional-trust-bundle-file}} or the equivalent RHCS Terraform provider field.

*CA certificate:* [Current-IT-Root-CAs.pem|https://certs.corp.redhat.com/certs/Current-IT-Root-CAs.pem] from [certs.corp.redhat.com|https://certs.corp.redhat.com/].

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* {{rosa describe cluster -c aipcc-arc}} shows the additional trust bundle is set.
* A pod in any namespace can validate TLS connections to RH-internal endpoints.

items.fromString:
*Goal:* As a release engineer, I want the ARC ROSA cluster to trust Red Hat's internal CA, so that workloads can connect to internal TLS services.

*Background:* The ARC ROSA cluster has TGW connectivity to the RH internal network, but containers only trust public CAs by default. OpenShift's cluster-wide proxy config accepts a custom CA bundle, which the built-in CA bundle injector then distributes to any namespace on demand.

*CA certificate:* [Current-IT-Root-CAs.pem|https://certs.corp.redhat.com/certs/Current-IT-Root-CAs.pem] from [certs.corp.redhat.com|https://certs.corp.redhat.com/].

*Implementation:*

IaC in {{k8s-arc/manifests/trusted-ca/}}:

# {{rh-it-root-ca.pem}} — the RH IT root CA PEM, committed from the URL above.
# {{kustomization.yaml}} — generates a {{custom-ca-bundle}} ConfigMap in {{openshift-config}} containing the PEM as {{ca-bundle.crt}}.
# {{proxy.yaml}} — sets {{spec.trustedCA.name: custom-ca-bundle}} on the cluster-wide {{Proxy}} resource.

CI applies via {{oc apply -k manifests/}}, which includes this subdirectory.

To refresh the cert after a rotation, re-download and commit:

{noformat}curl -fsSL -o manifests/trusted-ca/rh-it-root-ca.pem \
  https://certs.corp.redhat.com/certs/Current-IT-Root-CAs.pem{noformat}

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* The cluster proxy ({{proxy/cluster}}) has {{trustedCA}} set.
* A ConfigMap labeled {{config.openshift.io/inject-trusted-cabundle: "true"}} in any namespace gets populated with a bundle that includes the RH IT root CA.

*Goal:* As a release engineer, I want the ARC ROSA cluster to trust Red Hat's internal CA, so that workloads can connect to internal TLS services.

*Background:* The ARC ROSA cluster has TGW connectivity to the RH internal network, but containers only trust public CAs by default. OpenShift's cluster-wide proxy config accepts a custom CA bundle, which the built-in CA bundle injector then distributes to any namespace on demand.

*Implementation:*

# Create a ConfigMap in {{openshift-config}} containing the RH IT root CA PEM:

{noformat}oc create configmap custom-ca-bundle \
  --from-file=ca-bundle.crt=/path/to/rh-it-root-ca.pem \
  -n openshift-config{noformat}

# Patch the cluster-wide proxy to reference it:

{noformat}oc patch proxy/cluster --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"trustedCA":{"name":"custom-ca-bundle"}}}'{noformat}

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* The cluster proxy ({{proxy/cluster}}) has {{trustedCA}} set.
* A ConfigMap labeled {{config.openshift.io/inject-trusted-cabundle: "true"}} in any namespace gets populated with a bundle that includes the RH IT root CA.

*Do not edit this template directly. Instead, copy this Task, update the title, and fill in the relevant sections below.* All access requests must be tracked in Jira for security, compliance, and audit purposes. Requests made through Slack, email, or other ad-hoc channels are not considered valid unless captured here.

All approvals, decisions, and provisioning steps must be recorded in the created Task. Incomplete requests or missing approvals may delay or block access. *Access may be reviewed or revoked if it is no longer required.*

*HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE*

# Copy this Task and ensure it is linked under AIPCC-10105.
# {color:#de350b}*Update the Task title using this format: Grant (*{color}{color:#de350b}*_System_*{color}{color:#de350b}*) Access for (*{color}{color:#de350b}*_User_*{color}{color:#de350b}*) to (*{color}{color:#de350b}*_Resource_*{color}{color:#de350b} */* {color}{color:#de350b}*_Group_*{color}{color:#de350b} */* {color}{color:#de350b}*_Tenant_*{color}{color:#de350b}*).*{color}
# Fill in all required sections. Failing to fill required section will result in delays in processing the request.
# Provide a business justification; explain clearly why this access is needed. Access is granted only when there is a concrete, work-related need.
# Ensure any required approvals are provided as comments on the created Task.
# Once everything is in place ping {{@aipcc-support}} in {{#forum-aipcc}} slack channel for review.

Access to AIPCC-owned Quay repositories and Konflux tenants follows the same request and approval process and is granted at the same time. If you are unsure whether you need the access, do not request it. Requests without a clear justification may be denied. Any access beyond read-only requires both a business justification and manager approval.

Please provide:

* *Justification for access*: _(be specific about what you need to do in Quay and/or Konflux and why)_

items.fromString:
Document how users configure a private PyPI index for pip prefetch using PIP_INDEX_URL (Hermeto PR #1658: https://github.com/hermetoproject/hermeto/pull/1658).

Hermeto uses pip's precedence: requirements.txt --index-url > PIP_INDEX_URL > PyPI default

In hermetic Konflux builds, prefetch runs outside the base image, so pip.conf is not available. PIP_INDEX_URL lets teams set the index once on the prefetch step instead of adding --index-url to every requirements.txt.

*Work*

* Update docs/modules/building/pages/prefetching-dependencies.adoc (pip custom index section)
* Document precedence and recommend PIP_INDEX_URL for private indexes
* Add a taskRunSpecs example for the prefetch-dependencies step
* Keep --index-url in requirements as the per-file option
* Note the minimum Hermeto / prefetch task version

Blocked by: AIPCC-21291 (Konflux prefetch pipeline rollout)

Related: AIPCC-20093, AIPCC-21291, https://github.com/konflux-ci/build-definitions/issues/3680

items.fromString: Set min_release_age: 0 for amd-quark and pin version in requirements.txt

AMD regularly re-tags releases on GitHub (e.g. v0.12 was re-pushed 9 hours after the original release), and the GitLab mirror sync refreshes the commit timestamp. This causes fromager's 3-day release-age cooldown to block resolution even when the upstream release is days old.

To prevent recurring cooldown failures for amd-quark:

1. Set min_release_age: 0 in overrides/settings/amd_quark.yaml to permanently bypass the cooldown. This is necessary because the GitLab mirror sync date is always newer than the actual upstream release date, and AMD's re-tagging behavior makes the tag timestamp unreliable.

2. Pin amd-quark==0.12 in collections/torch-2.11.0/rocm7.14-ubi9/requirements.txt (not just constraints.txt) to make the version explicit at the requirements level rather than relying solely on constraint resolution.

h3. Summary

Mirror all versions of nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13 from the NVIDIA PyPI index to our internal Pulp repository. This is the CUDA 13 native library companion to nvidia-cutlass-dsl, required by vLLM for FA4 kernel generation via CuTe DSL. Related to AIPCC-18523 which mirrored nvidia-cutlass-dsl and nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base.

h3. Background

nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13 provides the CUDA 13–specific native libraries for the CUTLASS DSL package. It is an optional dependency of nvidia-cutlass-dsl via the {{[cu13]}} extra ({{pip install nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]}}). vLLM 0.24.0 on cuda13.0-ubi9 requires this package.

h3. Package: nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13

* *Versions to mirror:* 4.4.0, 4.4.1, 4.4.2, 4.5.0, 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.5.3, 4.6.0 (all available versions)
* *Wheels per version:* arch-specific wheels (cp310-cp314 + cp314t x aarch64/x86_64)
* *Source:* [https://pypi.nvidia.com/nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13/|https://pypi.nvidia.com/nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13/]
* *Destination:* [https://private.console.redhat.com/api/pulp-content/rhai/cuda-pypi/simple/nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13/|https://private.console.redhat.com/api/pulp-content/rhai/cuda-pypi/simple/nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13/]

items.fromString: https://github.com/IST-DASLab/qutlass/pull/12
items.toString: Migrate QuTLASS kernels used by vLLM to torch Stable ABI

This PR is to continue the libtorch stable ABI migration (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26946) for vLLM.

Migrates the qutlass kernels used by vLLM from unstable libtorch C++ APIs to PyTorch’s stable ABI (torch::stable::, STABLE_TORCH_LIBRARY_, AOTI shims). This enables qutlass to ship as an abi3 extension (_qutlass_C.so) alongside vLLM’s other stable targets (e.g. _C_stable_libtorch), so the extension can be built against a narrower libtorch surface and remain compatible across PyTorch minor versions.

Migration progress using the Audit Python extension [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/):
```
 -- extensions --
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=88, unstable=0)
    [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=0, unstable=72)
    [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok               ] _flashmla_extension_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=0, unstable=68)
    [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so  (stable_shim=72, unstable=0)
--> [STABLE  ] [abi3-ok               ] _qutlass_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=60, unstable=0)
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] cumem_allocator.abi3.so
    [NO-TORCH] [abi3-ok               ] spinloop.abi3.so
    [UNSTABLE] [uses-private-api      ] third_party/deep_gemm/_C.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so  (stable_shim=0, unstable=57)
    [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa2_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=0, unstable=84)
    [UNSTABLE] [abi3-ok               ] vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa3_C.abi3.so  (stable_shim=0, unstable=80)
```

I have not gained access to Blackwell GPUs yet, so I have not been able to run unit test locally to test the migration, I have only tested that the build work and is stable. I opened the vLLM PR https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47879 to test the changes against the vLLM CI. 


cc @Harry-Chen @janeyx99 @LopezCastroRoberto

Note @LopezCastroRoberto, this migrated the kernels used by vLLM to the torch Stable ABI, but I think there are more that are still unstable. If you would like me to do a full migration, I can follow up this PR with one that migrates the rest of the kernels.

[4844775539] Upstream Reporter: Reshmi Aravind
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}PR #1241 fixes one part of #1214: resolution failures now include the dependency path in the exception message body. For example, a `ResolverException` raised for a transitive dependency can now include:

`(dependency chain: its-hub==1.0 -> reward-hub==2.0 -> vllm==3.0 -> flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1)`

That makes the actual unresolved requirement and the chain that pulled it in visible in the error text.

However, as noted by Rohan in review of #1241, this does not fix the other half of #1214: the log line prefix itself can still be misleading.

Original example:

`ERROR its-hub: Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 with constraint flashinfer-python==0.6.11.post2 ...`

The `its-hub:` prefix comes from the logging context, specifically `requirement_ctxvar` / `req_ctxvar_context()` in `src/fromager/log.py`, via `FromagerLogRecord.getMessage()`. That prefix reflects whichever requirement context is active when the log record is created. For propagated bootstrap errors, that context is not guaranteed to identify the actual failing requirement, or even the immediate parent that introduced the failing dependency.

## Scope for a fix

This is broader than #1241 because:

* The misleading prefix is produced by shared logging infrastructure, not by `ResolverException` formatting itself.
* The issue is not specific to resolver failures. Any exception raised from a bootstrap phase can be logged under a misleading requirement context if the active `requirement_ctxvar` does not match the real failing item.
* A complete fix likely requires deciding how propagated bootstrap exceptions should carry or restore their failing `WorkItem` context when they are ultimately logged.

## Possible directions

Rohan, please let me know if one of these sounds acceptable, or if you had a different approach in mind:

1. Propagate structured failing-item context with bootstrap exceptions, including `item.req`, `item.resolved_version`, and `item.why_snapshot`, and use that context when logging the final failure.

items.toString:
[4844775539] Upstream Reporter: Reshmi Aravind
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}PR #1241 fixes one part of #1214: resolution failures now include the dependency path in the exception message body. For example, a `ResolverException` raised for a transitive dependency can now include:

`(dependency chain: its-hub==1.0 -> reward-hub==2.0 -> vllm==3.0 -> flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1)`

That makes the actual unresolved requirement and the chain that pulled it in visible in the error text.

However, as noted by Rohan in review of #1241, this does not fix the other half of #1214: the log line prefix itself can still be misleading.

Original example:

`ERROR its-hub: Unable to resolve requirement specifier flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 with constraint flashinfer-python==0.6.11.post2 ...`

The `its-hub:` prefix comes from the logging context, specifically `requirement_ctxvar` / `req_ctxvar_context()` in `src/fromager/log.py`, via `FromagerLogRecord.getMessage()`. That prefix reflects whichever requirement context is active when the log record is created. For propagated bootstrap errors, that context is not guaranteed to identify the actual failing requirement, or even the immediate parent that introduced the failing dependency.

* The misleading prefix is produced by shared logging infrastructure, not by `ResolverException` formatting itself.

* A complete fix likely requires deciding how propagated bootstrap exceptions should carry or restore their failing `WorkItem` context when they are ultimately logged.

2. Introduce a bootstrap-specific exception wrapper that records the failing `WorkItem` and dependency chain, then make top-level error logging use that instead of relying only on `requirement_ctxvar`.
3. Clear or suppress the automatic requirement prefix for final propagated bootstrap errors when the message already includes an explicit dependency chain, to avoid presenting a misleading package prefix.

This should be handled in a focused follow-up PR because changing `requirement_ctxvar` behavior affects shared logging behavior across phases, not only dependency resolution.{quote}

h3. Package update request for frozen RHOAI 3.4 index

h4. Packages

||Package||Current version||Target version||
|diffusers|0.37.1|0.38.0|
|safetensors|0.7.0|0.8.0|

safetensors 0.8.0 is required because diffusers 0.38.0 has a hard dependency on {{safetensors>=0.8.0-rc.0}}.

h4. Justification

*CVE-2026-44827* (CVSS 8.8, Important) — Diffusers: Arbitrary Code Execution via malicious model loading. In diffusers 0.37.0, {{DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained()}} can silently execute a {{None.py}} file from a malicious Hugging Face Hub repository, bypassing the {{trust_remote_code}} safeguard. Fixed in diffusers 0.38.0.

RHOAIENG tracking tickets: RHOAIENG-75752, RHOAIENG-75753, RHOAIENG-75750, RHOAIENG-75742

h4. Priority level

*High* — CVE remediation (CVSS 8.8, arbitrary code execution). Due date on RHOAIENG tickets: 2026-08-05.

h4. Target index version

RHOAI 3.4

h4. Variant(s) affected

* {{cuda13.0-ubi9}} — currently has diffusers 0.37.1, safetensors 0.7.0
* {{rocm6.4-ubi9}} — currently has diffusers 0.37.1, safetensors 0.7.0

h4. Impact assessment

*No new dependencies introduced.* Both packages are already in the 3.4 index — this is a version bump only. Both target versions (diffusers 0.38.0, safetensors 0.8.0) are already built and available on the RHOAI 3.5 indexes (cuda13.0-ubi9 and rocm7.14-ubi9).

The safetensors 0.8.0 constraint was already resolved for RHOAI 3.5 in AIPCC-15624. safetensors 0.8.0 is backwards-compatible — all other consumers in the index accept {{>=0.3.1}} or {{>=0.4.3}}.

h4. Affected images

* {{rhoai/odh-th06-cuda130-torch210-py312-rhel9}}
* {{rhoai/odh-th06-cuda130-torch291-py312-rhel9}}
* {{rhoai/odh-th06-rocm64-torch291-py312-rhel9}}

h4. Next steps

Once the packages are available on the 3.4 index, we will update {{requirements.txt}} in the affected universal training image directories and submit a PR to the rhds rhoai-3.4 branch.

h4. When comparing the benchmark results of Hermetic 2.13 and Upstream RHEL 2.13 we observe that the compilation time is consistently more across the all the configs, suites and modes. We observe that 6 out of 11 configs shows >5% delta. The table below gives complete info on the delta observed across different configs, suite and mode.

||Config||Suite||Mode||no of models||2.13 rc4 Hermetic (ms)||2.13 rc14 Upstream RHEL (ms)||Delta||
|dynamic|torchbench|training|12|5.029|4.723|-6.1%|
|dynamic|torchbench|inference|19|2.296|1.960|-14.6%|
|no_cudagraphs|torchbench|inference|21|5.217|4.943|-5.3%|
|with_cudagraphs|huggingface|training|27|16.334|15.462|-5.3%|
|with_cudagraphs|torchbench|training|12|4.193|3.713|-11.4%|
|with_cudagraphs|torchbench|inference|19|5.143|4.744|-7.8%|

h4. Dockers used: 


{noformat}  v2.13_hermeic_rc14: quay.io/aipcc/pytorch/hermetic-cuda:cuda-x86_64_rhel9_6_pytorch_v2.13.0-rc14_git3e3e24bd95b_cuda13_0_v37.2.0_20260702_2645989621
  v2.13_upstream_rc14: quay.io/aipcc/pytorch:rhel9_6_pytorch_v2.13.0-rc14_git3e3e24b_cuda13_0{noformat}


The possible reason is because of the way triton wheels are built. We use gcc build which bloats the size of libtriton.so file. As this file is loaded for the first run the compilation time increases.

Possible fix: build the triton using clang instead of gcc this decreases the debug logs and decreases the size of the so file. Upstream is building using clang. Re-run the perf once the clang triton wheels are uploaded to the index and check if the issue reproduceable. 

Attaching compilation_time.csv and compilation_time.png for reference.

Comparison logs: [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1s0DvWpWhvHHZh84d2BCu69sQ2zjTdTE8?usp=sharing|https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1s0DvWpWhvHHZh84d2BCu69sQ2zjTdTE8?usp=sharing|smart-link]

pytorch_2.13 pytorch_perf
This work item clones AIPCC-19488

During PyTorch v2.12.1 perf runs we compared our hermatic docker and upstream image and found that 9 out of ~310 combinations (model+configs) in hermetic wheels has lower torch.compile speedup wrt eager than upstream RHEL wheels by more than 5%.

*Dockers used:*

Hermetic Docker: {{quay.io/aipcc/pytorch/hermetic-cuda:cuda-x86_64_rhel9_6_pytorch_v2.12.1_git7269437_cuda13_0_v36.2.0_20260624_2626827685}}  

Upstream Docker (RHEL): {{quay.io/aipcc/pytorch:rhel9_6_pytorch_v2.12.1_gitunknown_cuda13_0}} 


Regressions are seen mostly in *TorchBench suite* (8 out of 9 models). Of the 8 regressing models 5 occur in the training mode. The only model which has lower speedup in Huggingface suite is {{XLNetLMHeadModel}} and this occurs during infernece in aot_inductor with a delta of 6.8%.

More details on the regressing models and deltas observed are shown in the table below:


||Config||Suite||Mode||Model||v2.12.1_hermetic||v2.12.1_upstream_rhel||delta_%||
|with_cudagraphs|torchbench|training|phlippe_resnet|1.374×|1.966×|43.1%|
|with_cudagraphs|torchbench|training|phlippe_densenet|1.653×|2.343×|41.7%|
|dynamic|torchbench|training|phlippe_resnet|1.369×|1.907×|39.3%|
|dynamic|torchbench|training|phlippe_densenet|1.635×|2.208×|35.0%|
|with_cudagraphs|torchbench|inference|maml|0.014×|0.017×|20.1%|
|dynamic|torchbench|inference|phlippe_densenet|2.131×|2.342×|9.9%|
|dynamic|torchbench|training|dlrm|1.396×|1.533×|9.9%|
|aot_inductor|huggingface|inference|XLNetLMHeadModel|1.399×|1.495×|6.8%|
|dynamic|torchbench|inference|maml|0.015×|0.015×|5.1%|



Creating this ticket to investigate further. See attached {{hermetic_slower_than_upstream.png}}, {{hermetic_slower_than_upstream.csv}} for the reference also check out {{per_model_*.csv}} in the [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CfASanALr1tTteIatVMly5fCfgRoHhsW|https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CfASanALr1tTteIatVMly5fCfgRoHhsW|smart-link]  for breakdowns.

items.fromString:
Tracking ticket for wheels that are missing or had to be removed from CUDA 13.x (13.0, 13.2, 13.3/Rubin) builder variants due to upstream incompatibilities. These should be re-added as upstream fixes become available.

h2. Removed wheels

h3. cupy-cuda13x (Rubin / CUDA 13.3)

{{cupy-cuda13x==14.1.1}} (latest available) fails to compile against CUDA 13.3 {{cusparse.h}} headers. The issue is that cupy defines {{CUSPARSE_SPGEAM_ALG_DEFAULT}} as a preprocessor macro ({{#define CUSPARSE_SPGEAM_ALG_DEFAULT 0}}) while CUDA 13.3's {{cusparse.h}} now defines {{cusparseSpGEAMAlg_t}} as a proper enum containing that same symbol, causing a conflict.

*Error:* {{cusparse.cpp:1211:41: error: expected identifier before numeric constant}}

*Action:* Removed from {{collections/torch-2.11.0/rubin-ubi9/}} requirements and constraints. Re-add once upstream cupy releases a CUDA 13.3-compatible version.

*Note:* cupy-cuda13x 14.1.1 builds fine against CUDA 13.0 and 13.2 — only 13.3 is affected.

h2. Missing wheels (CUDA 13.0+)

h3. tensorflow (CUDA 13.0, 13.2, Rubin)

TensorFlow is present in the CUDA 12.9 collection but absent from all CUDA 13.x variants. TensorFlow does not yet support CUDA 13.x.

h2. Minimal variants (no prebuilt torch wheels yet)

The following variants have minimal requirement sets (no torch, vLLM, flash-attn, xformers, etc.) because prebuilt torch wheels are not yet available:

* *cuda13.2-ubi9* — awaiting CUDA 13.2 torch wheels
* *rubin-ubi9* — awaiting CUDA 13.3 / Rubin torch wheels

Once torch wheels are available for these variants, the full requirement sets (matching cuda13.0-ubi9) should be populated.

Tracking ticket for wheels that are missing or had to be removed from CUDA 13.x (13.0, 13.2, 13.3/Rubin) builder variants due to upstream incompatibilities. These should be re-added as upstream fixes become available.

h2. Removed wheels

h3. cupy-cuda13x (Rubin / CUDA 13.3)

{{cupy-cuda13x==14.1.1}} (latest available) fails to compile against CUDA 13.3 {{cusparse.h}} headers. The issue is that cupy defines {{CUSPARSE_SPGEAM_ALG_DEFAULT}} as a preprocessor macro ({{#define CUSPARSE_SPGEAM_ALG_DEFAULT 0}}) while CUDA 13.3's {{cusparse.h}} now defines {{cusparseSpGEAMAlg_t}} as a proper enum containing that same symbol, causing a conflict.

*Error:* {{cusparse.cpp:1211:41: error: expected identifier before numeric constant}}

*Action:* Removed from {{collections/torch-2.11.0/rubin-ubi9/}} requirements and constraints. Re-add once upstream cupy releases a CUDA 13.3-compatible version.

*Note:* cupy-cuda13x 14.1.1 builds fine against CUDA 13.0 and 13.2 — only 13.3 is affected.

h3. tensorboard (Rubin / CUDA 13.3)

Tensorboard uses Bazel for its build, which requires network access to fetch dependencies (rules_nodejs, bazel-gazelle, etc.) from GitHub. The builder runs in a network-isolated environment, so these fetches fail with 504 Gateway Timeout or 404 errors.

*Error:* {{bazel fetch}} fails — {{GET returned 504 Gateway Time-out}} for {{bazel-gazelle-v0.33.0.tar.gz}}

*Action:* Removed both {{tensorboard==2.13.0}} and {{tensorboard}} (latest) from {{collections/torch-2.11.0/rubin-ubi9/requirements.txt}}. This is a builder infrastructure limitation, not a CUDA 13.3 incompatibility — tensorboard likely has the same issue on other variants but was already built and cached there.

h2. Missing wheels (CUDA 13.0+)

h3. tensorflow (CUDA 13.0, 13.2, Rubin)

TensorFlow is present in the CUDA 12.9 collection but absent from all CUDA 13.x variants. TensorFlow does not yet support CUDA 13.x.

h2. Minimal variants (no prebuilt torch wheels yet)

The following variants have minimal requirement sets (no torch, vLLM, flash-attn, xformers, etc.) because prebuilt torch wheels are not yet available:

* *cuda13.2-ubi9* — awaiting CUDA 13.2 torch wheels
* *rubin-ubi9* — awaiting CUDA 13.3 / Rubin torch wheels

Once torch wheels are available for these variants, the full requirement sets (matching cuda13.0-ubi9) should be populated.
